title: Order the edit loop
scenario: You have four versions of a product shot. One composition is right; the background colour is slightly off and the label area needs a small replacement. Instead of another round of re-rolls, you decide to work by editing — one disciplined loop from foundation to finished image.
task: Order the steps of the edit loop so each pass changes one thing and keeps everything else intact.
steps: Generate a small batch — two to four candidates — and choose a direction.
Pick the closest candidate as your foundation — not the perfect one.
Name exactly one change you want to make.
Apply it as an edit: describe the change for the whole image, or mark the region and describe its replacement.
Compare the new version with the previous one and keep the better of the two.
Only if the change spread too far: revert, then take a smaller step from the better version.
hints: A foundation comes before fine-tuning — pick the closest candidate first.
One variable per pass; anything else is a re-roll wearing a disguise.
explanation: The loop is: choose a foundation, name one change, apply it as an edit, compare, keep the better version. Order matters because each step depends on the previous one — you cannot compare versions you did not keep, and you cannot name a change until a foundation exists. Run in order, the loop turns iteration into a series of comparable decisions instead of a slot machine.
